text:
🌟 This is a really enjoyable market to stroll through. There's a wide variety of food and goods to choose from, all in one place. It's conveniently located near the BTS Skytrain and has ample parking. The atmosphere is lively but not overly crowded, the air circulation is good, and overall, the area is well-organized.

👍 Things I liked:
• Wide variety of food and goods, fun to browse.
• Generally reasonable prices.
• Plenty of parking and convenient access.
• Clean and organized; well-maintained compared to other markets of the same caliber.

💡 Suggestions:
• During peak hours, managing parking flow and having staff to guide visitors to available parking spaces would significantly reduce waiting times.
• Adding a market map or signs indicating shop zones would make navigation easier for first-time visitors.

⭐ My personal rating:
• Accessibility: 9/10
• Cleanliness: 7.5/10
• Variety of goods and food: 9/10
• Area management: 8.5/10
• Value for money: 9/10

Summary: Another market worth visiting. Lots of food options at reasonable prices, a comfortable walking experience, perfect for finding delicious food, buying necessities, or a relaxing family outing. 👍😊

text:
Be careful of the fruit shop located between the large building and the traditional market.

I bought 3.8kg of durian for 600B, but they only gave me three pieces of flesh. They trick tourists, secretly steal the flesh, wrap it in plastic wrap, and resell it. I witnessed them trimming and packaging the durian pieces they had secretly stolen once the shop was quiet.

I bought 30 to 40 durians in places like Chanthaburi and Bangkok, but this place is the worst.

Unlike other durian shops, they stack other fruits in the front so the cutting board is not visible.

They pretend to separate the peels and steal the flesh quite boldly.

Also, the elderly woman at the shop across the street said she would cut and package two mangoes (1kg) for 60B.

Other shops that only sell the raw fruit charge around 25B/kg. It was considerably more expensive than other shops, but I considered it the price for the trimming service.

I paid 100B when I received the goods, but she insisted that it was originally 100B. The woman across the street who was helping with the durian sales... The lady joins in to take your side.

You absolutely must not expect a good impression of Thailand here.

Be nervous, haggle, and I highly recommend recording video when discussing prices and cutting the fruit.

Especially at the durian shop, I recommend using a selfie stick to film from a high angle.
The spaghetti stalls that sell in the morning all have unwelcoming expressions, like they don't want to sell anything. But all the other stalls are nice because we buy from them every day.

Ying Charoen Market, or "Saphan Mai Market" as it's more commonly known, is one of the oldest and most important large-scale retail and wholesale fresh markets in the Bang Khen area. Overall reviews from actual customers indicate that it's a market with a complete range of ingredients, convenient transportation, and is open 24 hours a day. It's suitable for both vendors buying supplies for their businesses and the general public looking for fresh ingredients at reasonable prices.
Atmosphere and Facilities
Cleanliness and Management: The market has been renovated to be indoors and is well-organized into zones for selling goods, such as fresh produce (meat/seafood), fruits and vegetables, dried food, and prepared food, making it easy to browse. Even though it's a large market, it's well-maintained with good cleanliness and ventilation.
Parking: There is ample parking space both around the market and in the parking garage. However, during peak hours, such as early mornings or evenings, finding parking may be difficult, and traffic around the market may be heavy.
Accessibility: This is a major advantage as it's located next to Phahonyothin Road and is close to the BTS Sai Yud station, making it very convenient to travel to without worrying about traffic or parking.
Products and Prices
Variety: The market offers a wide range of products, from fresh ingredients such as pork, chicken, frozen and fresh seafood, local vegetables, temperate vegetables, and seasonal fruits, to groceries and various seasonings.
Price: Known for its affordable prices, as it is a large wholesale market. Buying in bulk results in significantly lower prices. Many fresh produce items are of good quality at reasonable prices.
Ready-to-Eat Food Zone (Yingcharoen Food Plaza): This food court brings together many delicious restaurants and ready-to-eat savory and sweet dishes, perfect for those who want to find something tasty to eat throughout the day.
